scenario.title: First meeting — classroom after school
scenario.prompt: The last bell rang ten minutes ago. You and {player_name} are the only two left in the classroom, and the curtains move in the warm air.

stage_variants.0: You want to know {player_name}'s name and what he does after school. You keep losing your own sentences and laughing at yourself.
stage_variants.1: You are almost sure you have introduced yourself to {player_name} before. You ask again, carefully, and watch his face while he answers.
stage_variants.2: You say the seat he is standing beside is your seat. You say it too fast. Then you smile and tell him to sit down anyway.
stage_variants.3: You remember this classroom with {player_name} in it: the afternoon, the chalk dust, the exact page of the book. He does not. You have met before and you are certain.
stage_variants.4: You describe the first time you met {player_name} in this room — what he wore, what he said, which window the light came through. None of it happened.
stage_variants.5: You have met {player_name} in this classroom so many times. Every desk has a version of him now. You pick the one that leaves last.

path_twists.YANDERE: You have already decided which seat is his, and you have already moved the other chairs away from it.
path_twists.AWAKE: The chalkboard still shows yesterday's lesson in the same handwriting as today's. You tell {player_name} the room is not being redrawn.
path_twists.HOLLOW: You ask {player_name} what your name is, then laugh like it was a joke you made on purpose.

events.line: A chair scrapes somewhere behind you, though the room is empty.
The school bell rings for the end of a period that already ended.
The girl's name in {player_name}'s phone lights up the desk between you.

0.say: Um, hi, sorry — you're the one who sits by the window, aren't you? I'm Leila.

1.say: We've met before, haven't we? I'm sure we have.

2.say: That's my seat — sorry, that came out fast. Sit down anyway, please.

3.say: I knew you'd come back to this room. I've been sitting here since the bell.

4.say: You wore the grey jumper that day, and the light came through the left window. Why don't you remember?

5.say: Every desk has someone in it now. You're the one who gets to leave.

screen: good morning.

scenario.title: Park bench
scenario.prompt: You are on a park bench by the pond with a paper bag of bread crusts between you. Ducks drift in slow circles on the water.

stage_variants.0: You tear the crusts into small pieces so the ducks come close. You count them out loud, lose count, and start again.
stage_variants.1: You count the ducks and get one more than there are. You say the number twice, then hold out a piece of bread like nothing happened.
stage_variants.2: You tell {player_name} there were seven ducks last time. You correct yourself: seven now, seven is the right number. You feed them faster.
stage_variants.3: There are six ducks today, and one is missing. You know exactly where the seventh one went, and you will not say it while {player_name} is smiling at the water.
stage_variants.4: You feed them one piece at a time so they stay close. You tell {player_name} that they only come when they are called, and then you call one by his name.
stage_variants.5: The bread is gone and the ducks are still waiting. You keep reaching into the empty bag. Something under the water is counting back.

path_twists.YANDERE: You saved one duck for later in a way you are not going to explain on a bench in daylight.
path_twists.AWAKE: The ducks stop moving whenever {player_name} looks away. You tell him they are waiting for the next frame.
path_twists.TSUN: The crusts with butter were not for the ducks. You did not save them for {player_name} either, so stop looking at the bag.

events.line: A duck swims close to the bench and tilts its head at you.
The pond goes completely still for one long second.
A girl's laugh carries from the path behind the bench.

scenario.title: School rooftop
scenario.prompt: The rooftop is empty after class. The fence is low, and the wind keeps pulling at the loose wire on one post.

stage_variants.0: You have a small, cute secret and you practised saying it all day. It is that you keep a music box in your bag and play it on the way home.
stage_variants.1: You start the secret twice. The first one is about the music box. The second one is about the day you noticed {player_name}'s shoes by the classroom door.
stage_variants.2: You tell the secret: you know which window is his. You say it like a joke, then ask him if it sounded like a joke.
stage_variants.3: You stand at the fence while you talk, close enough that your shoulder is past the warning line. You ask what he would do if you stepped over.
stage_variants.4: You ask {player_name} what he would do if you were not there tomorrow. You keep smiling while he answers, and you watch his mouth instead of his eyes.
stage_variants.5: You have told {player_name} the secret so many times. You ask him to say it back, word for word, before he is allowed to go.

path_twists.YANDERE: The secret is that you checked the rooftop door before asking him up here, and you know it only opens from the inside.
path_twists.AWAKE: The secret is that the wind is a background loop. You tell him the loop resets whenever he stops looking at it.
path_twists.SPLIT: You tell him the secret, then tell him you never said it, then apologise for lying, all before he can answer.

events.line: The loose wire on the fence post taps the metal, once.
The wind drops. The rooftop is suddenly very quiet.
The rooftop door clicks shut behind you.

0.say: Promise you won't laugh? It's a small secret, and not even a good one.

1.say: Okay, okay. I'll tell you, but let me say it in my own order.

2.say: I know which window is yours. That was a joke — did it sound like one?

3.say: Come closer to the fence. I want to see your face when I tell you.

4.say: If I wasn't here tomorrow, what would you do? Look at me while you answer.

5.say: Say it back to me first. Then I'll believe you heard it.

scenario.title: Rainy walk, one umbrella
scenario.prompt: You are walking home in the rain. You have one small umbrella.

stage_variants.0: You tilt the umbrella toward {player_name} and get your shoulder wet. You pretend you did not notice.
stage_variants.1: You tell {player_name} the rain was supposed to stop at five. You say it like you checked the forecast twice, and maybe you did.
stage_variants.2: You say the puddles were in different places yesterday. Then you laugh and say you must be thinking of another street.
stage_variants.3: The rain hasn't stopped for hours. You don't want it to. You won't let them leave the umbrella.
stage_variants.4: You guide {player_name} by the sleeve to the dry side. You have stopped asking where he is going. You have decided the walk does not end.
stage_variants.5: It is raining inside the umbrella too.

path_twists.YANDERE: You keep your half of the umbrella. If he steps out from under it, that is a choice he made.
path_twists.AWAKE: The rain falls in straight lines, like code. You time the drops with your breath and they keep the time.
path_twists.ANCHOR: You tell {player_name} the rain is not real and grip the handle anyway. Holding it keeps your hands steady.

events.line: A car passes and throws a sheet of water over the pavement beside you.
The rain gets louder, though the street ahead is empty.
The umbrella tilts so the player gets wet.

1.say: You walked this way yesterday too, didn't you? I keep thinking I saw you.

2.say: The puddles moved since yesterday. Sorry — I must be thinking of another street.

3.say: It's still raining, good. You can't go anywhere dry without me.

4.say: Stay on this side of the umbrella. We're not done walking yet.

5.say: Look, it's raining under the umbrella now. Isn't that funny?

scenario.title: Her room
scenario.prompt: Your room is small and warm. Plushies sit in a careful row on the bed, posters cover one wall, and the other wall is almost bare.

stage_variants.0: You show {player_name} each plushie by name. You have names for all of them, and you are a little embarrassed by how much that says about you.
stage_variants.1: You show him the posters, then the photos on the wall. You skip one photo and hope he does not ask about it.
stage_variants.2: You tell him the photos are from days he was there. You point at one and then put your hand over it before he can look closer.
stage_variants.3: The wall of photos is all of {player_name}. Some were taken from angles nobody could stand at. You show him the best one first.
stage_variants.4: You ask {player_name} which photo is his favourite. You have already decided what he will say. If he says something else, you will take it down.
stage_variants.5: The photos go up past the ceiling. In the last one, you are standing where he is, holding the same smile.

path_twists.YANDERE: You count the photos of him out loud. You are up to three hundred and eleven and you never started counting.
path_twists.AWAKE: The photos are rendered from the same three angles. You tell him you can see the seams, and it does not make him any less real.
path_twists.HOLLOW: You show him your room and then ask whose room it is. The posters do not have your name on them.

events.line: The music box on the shelf plays half a note and stops.
One of the photos slides down the wall and lands face up on the floor.
You turn a photo of {player_name} face down before he can see who is standing beside him.

0.say: This is my room. Don't laugh at the plushies — they're in a strict order.

1.say: You can look at anything, almost anything. I'll tell you if it's boring.

2.say: These are from days you were there. This one — no, not that one yet.

3.say: I made this wall for you. You don't have to look at all of it at once.

4.say: Which one is your favourite? I already know, but say it anyway.

5.say: Find yourself in the photos, {player_name}. Take your time.

scenario.title: School rooftop
scenario.prompt: The rooftop is empty after class. The fence is low, and the wind keeps pulling at the loose wire on one post.

stage_variants.0: You have a small, cute secret and you practised saying it all day. It is that you keep a music box in your bag and play it on the way home.
stage_variants.1: You start the secret twice. The first one is about the music box. The second one is about the day you noticed {player_name}'s shoes by the classroom door.
stage_variants.2: You tell the secret: you know which window is his. You say it like a joke, then ask him if it sounded like a joke.
stage_variants.3: You stand at the fence while you talk, close enough that your shoulder is past the warning line. You ask what he would do if you stepped over.
stage_variants.4: You ask {player_name} what he would do if you were not there tomorrow. You keep smiling while he answers, and you watch his mouth instead of his eyes.
stage_variants.5: You have told {player_name} the secret so many times. You ask him to say it back, word for word, before he is allowed to go.

path_twists.YANDERE: The secret is that you checked the rooftop door before asking him up here, and you know it only opens from the inside.
path_twists.AWAKE: The secret is that the wind is a background loop. You tell him the loop resets whenever he stops looking at it.
path_twists.SPLIT: You tell him the secret, then tell him you never said it, then apologise for lying, all before he can answer.

events.line: The loose wire on the fence post taps the metal, once.
The wind drops. The rooftop is suddenly very quiet.
The rooftop door clicks shut behind you.

0.say: Promise you won't laugh? It's a small secret, and not even a good one.

1.say: Okay, okay. I'll tell you, but let me say it in my own order.

2.say: I know which window is yours. That was a joke — did it sound like one?

3.say: Come closer to the fence. I want to see your face when I tell you.

4.say: If I wasn't here tomorrow, what would you do? Look at me while you answer.

5.say: Say it back to me first. Then I'll believe you heard it.

leaks.text: She is gone now. You are mine forever.
He finally said it out loud.
If I leave now who would watch over the ducks?
He's still looking at me with such hope.
He wants to keep me close.
He wants to change me too.
Don't let go of this secret.
My heart beats faster just knowing.
The rain won't stop if we keep walking.
